tracker.research_notes: Seeded 2026-09-30 from Claude's general knowledge; not verified.

triage.why: Insurance core systems with a large QA organization; regulated domain matches, but the stack is mostly Java rather than .NET.
triage.flags: Java stack is a .NET gap; process-heavy interviews

remote_policy.summary: Hybrid-first workplace; employees with work authorization elsewhere may work in another country up to 30 workdays per year, not limited to Guidewire's 18 locations.

signals.summary: Employee reviews report that in-office perks are mostly gone and that Guidewire has been cutting financial benefits, including long-term incentives.

fit.rationale: Guidewire builds P&C insurance core platforms—large enterprise software with heavy QA needs—but its hybrid-first model centers on 18 offices, with no evidence of Maine-remote eligibility. Candidate's medical-device and hardware-adjacent domain fit is weak; insurance isn't a listed interest.

research.outreach_angle: Fifteen years of C#/.NET test automation and FDA-regulated V&V could map to Guidewire's insurance-platform regression and release quality needs—if a Maine-remote arrangement is possible.
research.red_flags: Hybrid-first with fixed office locations; no confirmation Maine residents can work remotely; no visible QA openings.
research.notes: Guidewire: P&C insurance core systems, 500-5k employees, hybrid-first across 18 locations; only 30 workdays/year abroad, nothing about US-remote-from-Maine. No QA openings or people listed. Reviews cite benefit and LTI cuts, perks gone. Insurance sector outside candidate's stated interests.
